summary: Mutual NDA on counterparty paper that is largely aligned but has perpetual confidentiality, a GBP 100,000 per-breach liquidated sum, a one-sided assignment right, an IP assignment of improvements and feedback, and a strict carve-out evidence standard.

findings.quote: each Party, in its capacity as a Receiving Party, agrees and undertakes that it shall
findings.why: Obligations bind each Party as Receiving Party, and Disclosing Party is defined so either can be either.

findings.quote: which is designated as proprietary or confidential, or which reasonably ought to be understood as confidential given its nature and the circumstances of disclosure
findings.why: Definition covers marked or reasonably confidential information disclosed to the Receiving Party and includes derived notes and analyses.

findings.quote: use the Proprietary Information solely and strictly for the evaluation and execution of the Permitted Purpose and for no other commercial, developmental, or competitive purpose
findings.why: Use is limited to evaluating a prospective commercial transaction, close to the preferred wording.
findings.fallback_cited: Purpose limited to a named project, product evaluation or pilot.

findings.quote: that the Receiving Party can prove by contemporaneous written evidence:
findings.why: All four carve-outs are present but each must be proved by contemporaneous written evidence, stricter than the 'written records' or 'reasonable evidence' standard.
findings.draft_redline: that the Receiving Party can demonstrate by written records or other reasonable evidence:
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would be grateful if the evidence standard for the exclusions could be 'written records or other reasonable evidence', as a contemporaneous requirement is difficult to meet in practice.

findings.quote: the directors, officers, employees, individual contractors, and professional legal or financial advisers of a Party or its Affiliates who reasonably require access
findings.why: Representatives cover Affiliates and advisers but do not expressly include auditors or insurers.
findings.draft_redline: "Representatives" means the directors, officers, employees, individual contractors, and professional legal or financial advisers, auditors and insurers of a Party or its Affiliates who reasonably require access to Proprietary Information for the Permitted Purpose.
findings.note_to_counterparty: Please could the definition of Representatives expressly include auditors and insurers, who routinely need access to confidential information.

findings.quote: provide the Disclosing Party with prompt written notice thereof, to the extent legally permissible
findings.why: Compelled disclosure is permitted, notice is only where legally permissible, and cooperation is at the Disclosing Party's expense with reasonable efforts to obtain confidential treatment.
findings.fallback_cited: Obligation to use reasonable endeavours to obtain confidential treatment, at the Disclosing Party's cost.

findings.quote: copies of Proprietary Information created pursuant to routine, automated, and secure electronic data backup and archival procedures
findings.why: Return or destroy within 14 calendar days with officer-signed confirmation, with an exception for backups and legally required copies that stay confidential under 6.3.

findings.quote: remains the exclusive property of the Disclosing Party or its respective licensors
findings.why: Confidential Information and IP stay with the Disclosing Party and the only right is evaluation for the Permitted Purpose.

findings.quote: shall vest immediately upon creation in, and are hereby assigned to, the Disclosing Party with full title guarantee
findings.why: Assigns IP in improvements, derivatives and feedback created by the Receiving Party to the Disclosing Party, which would transfer Halyard's own developments when it is the recipient.
findings.draft_redline: Delete clause 5.3 and replace with: Each Party shall retain ownership of its own intellectual property and any modifications, improvements or feedback it creates, and no licence or assignment is granted other than the right to use Proprietary Information for the Permitted Purpose.
findings.note_to_counterparty: Clause 5.3 would transfer ownership of the receiving party's own developments and feedback; we propose each party keeps its own IP with no assignment.

findings.quote: The Disclosing Party makes no express or implied representations or warranties regarding the completeness, accuracy, efficacy, or suitability of any Proprietary Information disclosed hereunder.
findings.why: Mutual as-is disclaimer with no warranty from Halyard and no fraud exclusion removed.

findings.quote: shall continue in force for a period of twelve (12) months, unless terminated earlier by either Party upon giving thirty (30) days' prior written notice
findings.why: A 12-month term with 30 days' notice falls within the 1 to 3 year acceptable range.

findings.quote: continue in perpetuity with respect to all Proprietary Information disclosed under this Agreement, and each Party shall remain bound by such obligations indefinitely
findings.why: Confidentiality is perpetual for all information, not limited to Trade Secrets.
findings.draft_redline: Notwithstanding expiry or earlier termination, the confidentiality obligations shall survive for three (3) years after expiry or termination, save that Proprietary Information that constitutes a trade secret shall remain protected for as long as it remains a trade secret.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We propose a three-year survival period, with trade secrets protected for as long as they remain trade secrets.

findings.quote: the Disclosing Party shall be entitled to seek injunctive relief, specific performance, and other available equitable remedies from any court of competent jurisdiction without the necessity of proving actual damages or posting any bond
findings.why: Mutual 'entitled to seek' equitable relief without bond.
findings.fallback_cited: 'Entitled to seek' rather than 'entitled to'; no requirement to post a bond.

findings.quote: an agreed liquidated sum of £100,000 for each such breach
findings.why: Imposes a fixed per-breach liquidated payment of GBP 100,000 on the Receiving Party.
findings.draft_redline: Delete clause 8.2 in its entirety; remedies for breach remain damages and the equitable relief available under clause 8.1.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We are unable to agree a fixed per-breach sum and propose deleting clause 8.2, leaving general legal remedies and the equitable relief in clause 8.1.

findings.quote: the courts of England and Wales shall have exclusive jurisdiction to settle any dispute or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement
findings.why: English law and exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales.

findings.quote: except that Nordic Logix may assign this Agreement to an Affiliate or in connection with a corporate restructuring, merger, or sale of substantially all its business assets upon prior written notification
findings.why: Nordic Logix may assign on notice while Halyard needs prior written consent.
findings.draft_redline: Neither Party may assign, transfer, charge, subcontract, or novate any of its rights or duties under this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other Party.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We propose the assignment restriction apply equally to both parties, or alternatively that either party may assign to an Affiliate or successor on notice.

findings.quote: except to the extent strictly necessary to further the Permitted Purpose or as expressly permitted by mandatory statutory provisions
findings.why: Reverse engineering is prohibited but with an exception where necessary for the Permitted Purpose, which could allow reverse engineering of Halyard software.
findings.draft_redline: not copy, reproduce, reverse engineer, decompile, or disassemble any software, prototypes or materials provided by the Disclosing Party, except for copies reasonably necessary for the Permitted Purpose or as permitted by mandatory law.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We suggest limiting the exception to necessary copying and mandatory statutory rights so that the reverse engineering prohibition is not undermined.
